title: Rabbi Yirmeyah Shivshev
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: At the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Sotah, chapter 9, halakhah 15, Rabbi Yirmeyah “shivshev” and wore an olive wreath. Shmuel heard and said: “Better that his head had been cut off than that he did this.” It came about like an error issuing from a ruler. The commentators explain shivshev as cutting shoots to make the wreath.
Hyman rejects this: no Amora named Rabbi Yirmeyah lived in Shmuel’s time and died during his lifetime. He identifies the correct reading as that in Eichah Rabbah 5:16, Rabbi Yirmeyah of Shivshev.

And in Kohelet Rabbah 10:5: Rabbi Yirmeyah of Shivshta, and Hyman understands it as a place name. And in the book Chikrei Lev, part 2, p. 65, Hyman says that its author erred greatly in identifying him as the usual Rabbi Yirmeyah.

notes.text: The dispute is whether Shivshev is an action or a place-name. Hyman rejects a Yirmeyah who died in Shmuel’s lifetime; ושמת על פניו does not mean placing something on a face.

The consulted Kohelet Rabbah 10:5 directly has Yirmeyah de-Shavshta taking an olive wreath and Shmuel’s remark. Hyman’s proposed place-name reading, rejection of an action reading, assertion about Shmuel’s era and criticism of Chikrei Lev remain his confident argument; this parallel is not independent proof of absence or correction history.
